## Bug (reproduced, ground: my runs)
- `lambdify([x,y], -Mod(x,y))` → f(3,7) = -3, source `return -mod(x, y)` (correct)
- `lambdify([x,y], -Mod(x,y), modules=[])` → g(3,7) = 4, source `return -x % y` (WRONG: -x%y = (-x)%y = 4)
- modules=[] path uses `PythonCodePrinter` (lambdify.py ~line 812). Its `_print_Mul`
  (codeprinter.py:454) prints `Mul(-1, Mod(x,y))` as `-x % y` — Mod not parenthesized.

## Root cause (from diff old vs 1.14.0)
1. `sympy/printing/precedence.py`: old PRECEDENCE_VALUES lacks `"Mod": PRECEDENCE["Mul"]`
   (1.14.0 has it at line 42). So precedence(Mod) falls to default = Atom-ish (lowest),
   and `parenthesize(Mod_arg, prec)` never wraps it.
2. `codeprinter.py _print_Mul`: 1.14.0 added special-case for unary minus:
   `if len(a) == 1 and sign == "-": a_str = [self.parenthesize(a[0], 0.5*(PRECEDENCE["Pow"]+PRECEDENCE["Mul"]))]`
   (between Mul and Pow) — so `-Mod(x,y)` prints `-(x % y)`.
3. 1.14.0 precedence.py also has a Function-args check in `_print_Mul`-precedence fn
   (returns Mul precedence if any Function arg has precedence < Mul) and
   `could_extract_minus_sign()` instead of `_coeff_isneg`.

## Fix plan (minimal, source only, no tests)
- Add `"Mod": PRECEDENCE["Mul"]` to PRECEDENCE_VALUES in sympy/printing/precedence.py.
- Consider the unary-minus parenthesize tweak in codeprinter._print_Mul (needs PRECEDENCE import — already imported in 1.14; old file imports only `precedence`).
- Verify: lambdify modules=[] gives `-(x % y)` and g(3,7) = -3; run printing tests.

## Status
- [x] Reproduce bug
- [x] Locate cause (precedence.py Mod missing + codeprinter unary minus)
- [ ] Apply minimal fix
- [ ] Verify fix + run sympy/printing tests
